attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; boundary refinement of claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast and claim.law.pointer-walk-array-index-regression - applies when 2+ NEARBY fields (not just one) are read/written off the same walked or index-computed base pointer within one loop iteration or straight-line block.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast's counter-form (declare one typed alias per iteration, e.g. `T* p = base + i;`, then use `p->field` at every site) is proven safe for a walked loop touching ONE field per iteration, but does NOT extend to a walked/indexed base where 3+ NEARBY fields are read together: introducing the typed alias there can defeat MWCC's combined index-register addressing (lwzx/lfsx with a register operand that already sums a strength-reduced i*stride accumulator plus a per-field byte offset) and/or its single pre-folded pointer-plus-immediate-displacement construction, forcing a real regression even though the alias is declared once and used idiomatically. Two independent confirmations in world.c: (1) WorldSaveInitState's per-object snapshot loop reads WorldObj.parent and .pos[0..2] (4 fields) off `*wobjsp + i*60`; target computes `i*60` via a persistent per-iteration accumulator (+=60) and combines it with each field's byte offset (+24/28/32/36) via lwzx/lfsx indexed loads, reloading `*wobjsp` fresh at every one of the 4 field sites - a typed `WorldObj* wo = *wobjsp + i;` with `wo->parent`/`wo->pos[k]` regressed real 64->68 (register-pressure cascade from destroying the indexed-addressing shape). (2) WorldPsysActivate reads coltri.pos[0..2] (3 fields) off `ctris_base + ctriidx*40 + 8`; target pre-folds the +8 into ONE `addi` before three flat 0/4/8-displacement `lfs` loads, but a typed `struct coltri* ctri = ...; ctri->pos[k]` re-splits the +8 into each load's own displacement instead, regressing real 0->21. The verified-safe form for this multi-field case is the RAW walked pointer with offsetof-computed (not bare-hex) displacements per field - i.e. claim.law.offsetof-fused-immediate-counter's form, never a typed intermediate - even where the field count is small enough that a typed alias looks like the more natural/idiomatic C. Rule of thumb going forward: A/B a typed alias against the raw offsetof form whenever a walked or index-computed pointer feeds MORE THAN ONE field access within the same block; do not assume the single-field precedent transfers.
